reference.title: Barbell Standing Concentration Curl
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be read from this environment, gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Brace in the hinge; breathe out as the bar comes up, in as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 0.3 s squeeze, 2.4 s down

prescription.tempo: 1 s up, short squeeze, 2-3 s down
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: light; the upper arms and trunk must stay still, about 2 reps in reserve.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then a small amount of weight.

cues.text: Feet hip width, soft knees, hinge forward until the trunk is well inclined, back flat; underhand grip about shoulder width, arms hanging straight down.
Curl the bar up toward the face; the upper arms stay hanging still.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top.
Lower slowly to straight arms, upper arms still.
Keep the hinge and the brace for the next rep.

mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows hanging under the shoulders; lighten the bar.
Hold the hinge; only the forearms move.
Brace and hinge only as far as a flat back allows.
Straighten the arms fully at the bottom.

kinematics.norm: Full range from a straight arm to about 130-145 degrees (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: Palms up the whole rep with a straight bar (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: Upper arms hang vertically under the shoulders while the trunk is hinged (clinical opinion)
Bar clear of the legs and the head (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion)
Hinged trunk held still; bent-over positions load the lower back (Fenwick 2009)

cautions: Hold the brace and the hinge for the whole set; stand up and rest if the back starts to round.
Low-back pain: do a seated dumbbell concentration curl instead.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Lower back: smaller hinge or rest the free forearm on a bench (dumbbell version).
